title: 1.2 Ecology II: fieldwork, population estimation and limiting factors

q.Q1: Q1. A learner places ten 1 m2 quadrats on a 500 m2 field and counts 4, 6, 3, 5, 2, 7, 4, 5, 3, 6 daisies. Estimate the population.

q.Q2: Q2. Explain why a belt transect, not random quadrats, should be used to study how plants change from a forest edge into open grassland.

q.Q3: Q3. A learner catches 40 beetles, marks and releases them. A week later she catches 50, of which 8 are marked. Estimate the population.
q.Q4: Q4. State two assumptions of the capture–recapture method.

q.Q5: Q5. Describe and explain the stationary phase of a population growth curve.
q.Q6: Q6. Suggest why the zebra population in the Maasai Mara rises in years of good rain.

q.Q7: Q7. Plan how your class could estimate the number of grasshoppers in the school field and the cover of grass. Name methods, equipment and one source of error.

q.Exit ticket: Exit ticket. Write the Lincoln index formula.
